facts_of_case: The parties were married for three days before separating. They filed a petition under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act for divorce by mutual consent after over one year of separation.

legal_principles.principle: The statutory period of six months specified in Section 13B(2) is directory in nature.
legal_principles.held: However, if a Court comes to the conclusion that there is no chance of a reunion, it should not be powerless to waive the statutory period of six months so that the parties may not be subjected to further agony.

legal_principles.principle: All efforts for mediation/conciliation including efforts in terms of Order XXXIIA Rule 3 CPC/Section 23(2) of the Act/Section 9 of the Family Courts Act to reunite the parties have failed and there is no likelihood of success in that direction by any further efforts.
legal_principles.held: ii) all efforts for mediation/conciliation including efforts in terms of Order XXXIIA Rule 3 CPC/Section 23(2) of the Act/Section 9 of the Family Courts Act to reunite the parties have failed and there is no likelihood of success in that direction by any further efforts;

legal_principles.principle: The parties have genuinely settled their differences including alimony, custody of child or any other pending issues between the parties.
legal_principles.held: iii) the parties have genuinely settled their differences including alimony, custody of child or any other pending issues between the parties;

legal_principles.principle: The waiting period will only prolong their agony.
legal_principles.held: iv) the waiting period will only prolong their agony;

outcome.final_order: The High Court's order dismissing the Civil Revisional Application was upheld, and the requirement to wait six months before filing a petition for divorce was not waived.
